newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile sees 1997 economic growth at 5.75 pct.
newsitem.headline: Chile sees 1997 economic growth at 5.75 pct.

text.p: The Chilean budget projected that economic growth will slow to 5.75 percent from over seven percent in 1996, the Chilean government said.
The budget forecast that inflation will fall to 5.5 percent next year from a government target of 6.5 percent this year.
Chile's budget figures assume that copper prices will average $0.94 per pound next year, officials said.
Chile is the world's largest copper producer and the government takes a conservative view of copper prices when calculating the annual budget.
The government estimates tax income will be 5.7 trillion pesos, up 4.7 percent in real terms on 1996, said budget director Jos Pablo Arellano in a statement.

Government spending will grow 5.6 percent on 1996, with education and pensions among the priority areas, said Arellano. The budget, which will be sent Friday to Congress for approval, includes nearly 200 programs, he said.
"The main objective has been to maintain and increase the social effort which the government is making," he said.
The government's austerity efforts are reflected by the fact personnel and service expenses will only rise 4.5 percent next year, said Arellano.
